In this post, I analyze the relationship between the Brent Crude Oil index and US gas prices at the pump. I use time series forecasting with exogenous variables to test whether Brent Crude is a useful predictor of US gas prices.
```{r}
library(fpp3)
library(tidyverse)
library(fredr)
library(janitor)
library(future)
library(slider)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(tictoc)
library(arrow)
library(tidytext)
library(glue)
library(broom)

theme_set(
  theme_ipsum() +
    theme(
      axis.line.x.bottom = element_line(linewidth = .2),
      axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = .2)
    )
)

plan(multisession)

options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)

set.seed(1234)
```

This code pulls the data from FRED.
```{r}
#| eval: false
fred_df_raw <- c(
  "brent_crude" = "DCOILBRENTEU", #brent crude
  "us_consumer_gas" = "GASREGW" #us gas price
) |>
  map_dfr(fredr, .id = "series")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
fred_df_raw |>
  write_parquet(
    "/Users/conorotompkins/Documents/github_repos/ctompkins_quarto_blog/posts/us_gas_price_forecast/post_data/oil_prices_time_series.parquet"
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
fred_df_raw <-
  read_parquet(
    "/Users/conorotompkins/Documents/github_repos/ctompkins_quarto_blog/posts/us_gas_price_forecast/post_data/oil_prices_time_series.parquet"
  )
```

The results from FRED are stored in a dataframe (series, date, value)
```{r}
glimpse(fred_df_raw)
```

Here I clean up the dataframe and filter it so the begining and end of each series align. Brent Crude is measured daily, while the US gas price is measured weekly, so I aggregate the data to the year-week level.
```{r}
oil_prices <- fred_df_raw |>
  select(series, date, value) |>
  rename(price = value)

aligned_time_window <- oil_prices |>
  summarize(start_date = min(date), end_date = max(date), .by = series) |>
  summarize(start_date = max(start_date), end_date = min(end_date))

oil_prices <- oil_prices |>
  filter(between(
    date,
    aligned_time_window$start_date,
    aligned_time_window$end_date
  ))

oil_prices <- oil_prices |>
  mutate(date_week = yearweek(date)) |>
  summarize(price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(series, date_week)) |>
  arrange(series, date_week) |>
  mutate(flag_imputed_price = is.na(price)) |>
  fill(price, .by = series, .direction = "down")

oil_prices <- as_tsibble(oil_prices, key = series, index = date_week)

has_gaps(oil_prices) |> pull(.gaps) |> any() == FALSE

oil_prices |>
  filter(is.na(price)) |>
  count(series)

glimpse(oil_prices)
```

This plots the two series in a faceted chart. They follow each other closely.
```{r}
autoplot(oil_prices) +
  facet_wrap(vars(series), scale = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  guides(color = "none")
```

This calculates the week-over-week % change, and a % change indexed to the first observation, for each series. The WoW graph shows that US gas prices follow the Brent Crude index, but does not have as extreme highs and lows.
```{r}
oil_comparison <- oil_prices |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    wow_pct_change = (price - lag(price)) / price,
    price_indexed = price / first(price),
    .by = series
  ) |>
  mutate(
    decade = (year(date_week) %/% 10),
    decade = str_c(decade, "0s", sep = "")
  )

oil_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date_week, y = wow_pct_change, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-.1, .1)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(decade), scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Week-over-week % change",
    subtitle = "Brent Crude Oil and US Consumer Gas Price",
    x = "Date",
    y = "% change",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  scale_y_percent()
```

A basic scatterplot of the WoW % change of the two indexes shows that there is not a strong relationship.
```{r}
compare_wow <- oil_comparison |>
  select(series, date_week, wow_pct_change) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = wow_pct_change)

compare_wow |>
  ggplot(aes(us_consumer_gas, brent_crude)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Week-over-week % change",
    subtitle = "Brent Crude Oil and US Consumer Gas Price",
    x = "US Consumer Gas Price",
    y = "Brent Crude Oil"
  )

lm(us_consumer_gas ~ brent_crude, compare_wow)
```

This line graph of the indexed % change of each series shows that the two series were tightly coupled in the 2000s and 2020s, but diverged in the 19990s and 2010s.
```{r}
first_week <- min(oil_prices$date_week)

oil_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date_week, y = price_indexed, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(decade), scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = glue("Price of oil indexed to {first_week}"),
    subtitle = "Brent Crude Oil and US Consumer Gas Price",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Index",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  scale_y_percent()
```


This code decomposes the series into components and plots them.
```{r}
ts_components <- oil_prices |>
  model(
    stl = STL(
      price ~ season(period = "1 year")
    )
  ) |>
  components() |>
  rename(year_seasonality = `season_1 year`)

ts_components |>
  select(
    series,
    date_week,
    price,
    trend,
    year_seasonality,
    remainder,
    season_adjust
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(series, date_week)) |>
  mutate(
    name = factor(
      name,
      levels = c(
        "price",
        "season_adjust",
        "trend",
        "year_seasonality",
        "remainder"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  autoplot() +
  facet_wrap(vars(name, series), scale = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  guides(color = "none")
```

The two series are highly correlated across various decompositions of the time series.
```{r}
ts_components |>
  select(
    series,
    date_week,
    price,
    trend,
    year_seasonality,
    remainder,
    season_adjust
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(series, date_week)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(
    name = factor(
      name,
      levels = c(
        "price",
        "season_adjust",
        "trend",
        "year_seasonality",
        "remainder"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(us_consumer_gas, brent_crude)) +
  geom_point(size = .5, alpha = .1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(name), scales = "free")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
cv_size <- 52 * 4

cv_step <- 52 * 3
```

This cross-validates the `us_consumer_gas` series with chunks of `{r} cv_size` weeks of each series, stepping forward by `{r} cv_step` weeks. Then I train various models of different types, which I will then forecast and find the accuracy to determine which model structure is most appropriate.
```{r}
oil_prices |>
  count(series)

us_oil_prices <- oil_prices |>
  filter(date_week >= yearweek("2000 W1")) |>
  filter(series == "us_consumer_gas")

ts_cv <- us_oil_prices |>
  slide_tsibble(.size = cv_size, .step = cv_step)

brent_crude_exo <- oil_prices |>
  filter(series == "brent_crude") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(date_week, price) |>
  rename(brent_crude = price) |>
  mutate(
    brent_crude_lag1 = lag(brent_crude, 1),
    brent_crude_lag5 = lag(brent_crude, 5),
    brent_crude_lag10 = lag(brent_crude, 10),
    brent_crude_mean10 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ mean(.x), .before = 10),
    brent_crude_mean30 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ mean(.x), .before = 30),
    brent_crude_mean60 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ mean(.x), .before = 60),
    brent_crude_max10 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ max(.x), .before = 10),
    brent_crude_max20 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ max(.x), .before = 20),
    brent_crude_max30 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ max(.x), .before = 30),
  ) |>
  drop_na()

ts_cv <- left_join(ts_cv, brent_crude_exo)

ts_cv |>
  count(.id)

ts_cv |>
  as_tibble() |>
  summarize(
    start_date = min(date_week),
    end_date = max(date_week),
    .by = .id
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = start_date, xend = end_date, y = .id)) +
  geom_segment() +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(x = "Time window", y = "Cross-validation chunk")
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
tic()
ts_models <- ts_cv |>
  model(
    #simple models for benchmarking
    naive = NAIVE(price),
    dcmp = decomposition_model(
      STL(log(price + 1) ~ season(period = "1 year")),
      ETS(season_adjust ~ season("N"))
    ),
    mean_16 = MEAN(price, window(16)),
    mean_52 = MEAN(price, window(52)),
    #these ARIMA models constrain the seasonal PDQ
    dhr1_pdq = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 1) +
        PDQ(0, 0, 0)
    ),
    dhr3_pdq = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 3) +
        PDQ(0, 0, 0)
    ),
    dhr5_pdq = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        PDQ(0, 0, 0)
    ),
    dhr7_pdq = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 7) +
        PDQ(0, 0, 0)
    ),
    #these ARIMA models let the ARIMA() function search the parameter space for optimal values of P, D, Q
    dhr1_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 1)
    ),
    dhr3_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 3)
    ),
    dhr5_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5)
    ),
    dhr7_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 7)
    )
  )
toc()
```

```{r}
ts_models
```

Once the models are trained, I forecast 52 weeks ahead.
```{r}
#| cache: true
tic()
test_fc <- ts_models |>
  forecast(h = 52)
toc()
```

```{r}
test_fc
```

Then I calculate the accuracy of those forecasts
```{r}
#| cache: true
tic()
test_acc <- accuracy(
  test_fc,
  oil_prices,
  list(rmse = RMSE, crps_skill = skill_score(CRPS))
) |>
  arrange(series, desc(crps_skill))
toc()
```

```{r}
test_acc |>
  mutate(
    .model = reorder_within(
      x = .model,
      by = crps_skill,
      within = series
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = crps_skill, y = .model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(vars(series), scales = "free") +
  scale_y_reordered()
```

```{r}
recent_history <- oil_prices |>
  group_by(series) |>
  slice_tail(n = 60) |>
  ungroup()

us_acc <- test_acc |>
  filter(series == "us_consumer_gas") |>
  pull(.model)

test_fc |>
  filter(.id == max(.id)) |>
  mutate(.model = factor(.model, levels = us_acc)) |>
  autoplot(ts_cv) +
  facet_wrap(vars(.model), scales = "free_y") +
  guides(fill = "none", color = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-validated forecasts",
    subtitle = "Arranged most to least accurate",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Price"
  )

test_fc |>
  filter(.model == us_acc[1]) |>
  autoplot(ts_cv) +
  facet_wrap(vars(.id), scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = glue("Cross-validated forecasts of {us_acc[1]} model"),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Price"
  )
```

### Modelling US oil prices

#### Find reasonable horizon

Based on the cross-validated accuracy, the `dhr5_free` did the best. This code calculates the accuracy of `dhr5_free` and the best benchmark model `dcmp` at each index of the forecast horizon.
```{r}
#| cache: true
final_models <- ts_cv |>
  model(
    dcmp = decomposition_model(
      STL(log(price + 1) ~ season(period = "1 year")),
      ETS(season_adjust ~ season("N"))
    ),
    dhr5_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5)
    )
  )

# 4. Add horizon index
fc_h <- final_models |>
  forecast(h = 52) |>
  group_by(.id, .model) |>
  mutate(h = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  as_fable(response = "price", distribution = price)

# 5. Accuracy by horizon
acc_by_h <- accuracy(fc_h, oil_prices, by = c("h", ".model")) # one row per horizon & model
```

```{r}
acc_by_h |>
  select(h, .model, RMSE, MAPE) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(h, .model)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = h, y = value, color = .model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(name), scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Forecast error across forecast horizon",
    x = "Forecast horizon (weeks)",
    y = "Error",
    color = "Model"
  )
```

```{r}
#Accuracy by horizon and .id
acc_by_h_id <- fc_h |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(price_fc = price) |>
  left_join(
    oil_prices |>
      as_tibble() |>
      rename(price_actual = price),
    by = c("series", "date_week")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    error = price_actual - price_fc,
    abs_err = abs(error),
    ape = abs_err / price_actual # fractional (0–1); *100 for %
  ) |>
  group_by(.model, .id, h) |>
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(error^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

acc_by_h_id
```

Breaking the error graph out by cross-validation `.id` shows a similar pattern.
```{r}
#try a boxplot or ribbon chart instead of just line
#group by h, .model, .id
acc_by_h_id |>
  select(.id, h, .model, RMSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = h, y = RMSE, fill = .model, group = c(h))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(vars(.model), scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Forecast error (RMSE) across forecast horizon",
    subtitle = "By cross-validation chunk",
    x = "Forecast horizon (weeks)",
    y = "RMSE",
    fill = "Model"
  )
```

Based on RMSE and MAPE, a reasonable horizon is 12 weeks. The error increases significantly after that. Interestingly, `dcmp` and `dhr5_free` have similar curves until week ~32, when the error for `dhr5_free` decreases faster than `dcmp`.

Next I train additional models based on `dhr5_free` that consider various transformation of Brent Crude Oil as exogenous predictors.
```{r}
#| cache: true
tic()
models_cv_benchmark <- ts_cv |>
  model(
    dcmp = decomposition_model(
      STL(log(price + 1) ~ season(period = "1 year")),
      ETS(season_adjust ~ season("N"))
    ),
    dhr5_free = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5)
    )
  )

models_cv_exo <- ts_cv |>
  model(
    dhr5_free_bc = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_lag1 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_lag1
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_lag5 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_lag5
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_lag10 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_lag10
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_mean10 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_mean10
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_mean30 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_mean30
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_mean60 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_mean60
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_max10 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_max10
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_max20 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_max20
    ),
    dhr5_free_bc_max30 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_max30
    )
  )

models_cv_all <- left_join(
  models_cv_benchmark,
  models_cv_exo,
  by = join_by(.id, series)
)
toc()
```

```{r}
models_cv_all
```

Next I forecast the models 12 weeks ahead and find the accuracy.
```{r}
#| cache: true
tic()
cv_fc <- forecast(models_cv_all, ts_cv, horizon = 12)
toc()

tic()
cv_acc <- accuracy(
  cv_fc,
  oil_prices,
  list(rmse = RMSE, crps_skill = skill_score(CRPS))
) |>
  arrange(desc(crps_skill))
toc()

cv_acc
```

```{r}
best_model <- cv_acc |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  pull(.model)

cv_acc |>
  mutate(.model = fct_reorder(.model, crps_skill)) |>
  ggplot(aes(crps_skill, .model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-validated forecast accuracy",
    subtitle = "US Consumer Gas Price",
    x = "CRPS Skill",
    y = NULL
  )
```

This shows the last cross-validation forecast of the best model `{r} best_model`.
```{r}
cv_fc |>
  filter(.id == max(.id), .model == best_model) |>
  autoplot(ts_cv)
```

Finally, I refit `{r} best_model` against the entire training set and set up some future scenarios of Brent Crude Oil to use as predictors.
```{r}
#| cache: true
ts_train_final <- oil_prices |>
  filter(date_week >= yearweek("2000 W1")) |>
  filter(series == "us_consumer_gas") |>
  #slice_tail(n = cv_size) |>
  left_join(brent_crude_exo, by = join_by(date_week))

ts_model_final <- ts_train_final |>
  model(
    dhr5_free_bc_mean10 = ARIMA(
      log(price + 1) ~ fourier(period = 365.25 / 7, K = 5) +
        brent_crude_mean10
    )
  )
```

```{r}
final_fc_h <- 12

generate_horizon_exo <- function(x, price_vec) {
  horizon <- new_data(x, n = final_fc_h) |>
    mutate(brent_crude = price_vec)

  bind_rows(x, horizon) |>
    mutate(
      brent_crude_mean10 = slide_dbl(brent_crude + 1, ~ mean(.x), .before = 10)
    ) |>
    slice_tail(n = final_fc_h)
}

last_price <- oil_prices |>
  filter(date_week == max(date_week), series == "brent_crude") |>
  pull(price)

scenario_names <- c(
  glue("Decrease to ${last_price * .8}"),
  glue("Stabilize at ${last_price}"),
  glue("Increase to ${last_price * 1.2}")
)

exo_scenarios <- scenarios(
  generate_horizon_exo(
    ts_train_final,
    seq(last_price, last_price * .8, length.out = final_fc_h)
  ),
  generate_horizon_exo(
    ts_train_final,
    rep(last_price, final_fc_h)
  ),
  generate_horizon_exo(
    ts_train_final,
    seq(last_price, last_price * 1.2, length.out = final_fc_h)
  )
) |>
  set_names(scenario_names)

scenario_fc <- ts_model_final |>
  forecast(exo_scenarios) |>
  mutate(
    .scenario = fct_relevel(
      .scenario,
      scenario_names
    )
  ) |>
  select(.scenario, .model, series, price, .mean) |>
  mutate(
    intervals = hilo(price, 80),
    price_lower = intervals$lower,
    price_upper = intervals$upper
  )

scenario_fc

scenario_legend_text <- "Brent Crude Oil scenario"

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = ts_train_final |>
      slice_tail(n = 52 * .5),
    aes(x = date_week, y = price, colour = "History"),
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = scenario_fc,
    aes(
      x = date_week,
      ymin = price_lower,
      ymax = price_upper,
      fill = .scenario
    ),
    alpha = .3
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = scenario_fc,
    aes(x = date_week, y = .mean, colour = .scenario)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = glue("{final_fc_h} week forecast of US gas price at the pump"),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Price",
    fill = scenario_legend_text,
    color = scenario_legend_text
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_x_yearweek(date_breaks = "4 weeks") +
  scale_y_continuous(label = \(x) str_c("$", x))
```
